This question reminds me of my childhood. Kingdom Hearts was integral to my growing up for a lot of reasons.

When I ask myself this question, I don't really get an answer. Just a resounding void (not a painful or negative experience, just something that "is") inside. I feel content with this.

I look at almost everything that I've ever considered that could possibly answer this question (family, love, hope, freedom, progress, betterment of myself, knowledge, etc etc.) and the only thing that ever makes me think twice about it is really God (which encompasses, in my mind, all of those things). Just because I have history with that and know of it more than anything else.

But I am imperfect in seeking Him. I suppose that's part of what it means to seek Him, but at the same time, lacking true drive to commit myself to any thing (especially Him) leaves me wanting.

I desire an answer to this question of what I value most or what is most important to me, but at the same time, I am perfectly content with what I am now (in having a void where that answer is).

It's confusing, but I find how I am in most things is this: A paradox. Where I want one or the other, but am fine with either extreme. The middle is what I can't stand (where I'm not committed to either side of whatever options there are), but it's also where I find myself most often.

sigh, life is hard. But it's also so easy. ... Again. Paradox. I don't get it. Any of it. All I can really do is hope for change, even though my experience tells me that every time change happens. It's exciting, but then when change is done, whatever the situation is after it is nothing different from the situation before it had happened. Which again, is confusing, but whatever.

Maybe I'm desensitized to life. Or Jaded. Or something. Sorry if this sounds like rambling. It's all I've got. And I'm both ok and not ok with that.
